description.narrative:
Goal 1: TRANSFORMED MINDSETS: "We envision a future where militarised mindsets are transformed, where we have shifted dominant attitudes and beliefs that champion discriminatory and destructve forms of power".
Objectives
- Reframe security concepts to promote peace and security, including eliminating weapons and investing in community/social infrastructure. - Shift public attitudes about militarism by raising awareness of the devastating costs of war and promoting nonviolent conflict resolution. - Transform destructive gender norms by promoting equal partnerships, engaging men/boys as peace allies, and accepting complex gender identities. - Address and dismantle racist, privileged systems, practices, and colonial mentalities.
PROGRESS MARKERS 1.1 WILPF IS has increased the production/co-production (with other actors and institutions) of feminist knowledge showcasing linkages between gender justice and socio-economic justice that prioritises 'care' for people and the planet. 1.2 WILPF IS analysis, perspective and initiatives (standalone or joint) on gender, war, peace and security are able to influence discourse and stances of individuals including men, local communities, states, international, regional and local institutions. 1.3 WILPF facilitates enhanced, safe and sustained spaces to feminists, activists and WHRDs to participate, reflect and share contextual analysis on militarism, security and political economy. 1.4 WILPF IS is able to inspire and foster partnerships and collaborations with other movements, campaigns, networks and institutions - that challenge existing ideologies and mindsets around militarism, capitalism, neocolonialism, inequality and racism and advocate for feminist alternatives for society, community and environment.
Goal 2: VIOLENCE PREVENTED: "We envision a future where violence is prevented through peaceful and gender-responsive means that address root causes of conflict".
Objectives: - Prevent and eradicate gender-based violence in all its forms and from all spheres of life, both in times of conflict and peace. - Address and resolve conflicts through nonviolent, inclusive means, with justice and gender equality at the heart of conflict prevention. - Stigmatise weapons and harmful technology, cease arms race and redistribute military budgets for public good. - Hold governments, corporations, militaries and other actors accountable for human rights violations and abuses.
PROGRESS MARKERS 2.1 WILPF IS's advocacy holds states, multilateral institutions and private actors including corporations accountable for human rights violations and abuses due to the use and sale of weapons as well as of technologies. 2.2 WILPF IS's advocacy and critical feminist analysis contribute to the holistic implementation of the WPS agenda. 2.3 WILPF IS's advocacy and support contributes to a safe and enabling environment for feminists, human rights activists, women human rights defenders (WHRDs), LGBTIQ activists, peace and environment activists to be able to participate in multilateral bodies on WPS and human rights to influence peace and security matters. 2.4 WILPF Sections, Groups and Partners have enhanced capacity to produce gender-conflict analysis and advocate for gender justice, human rights and violence prevention. 2.5 WILPF's advocacy and campaigning has been able to influence perspectives and actions of states and civil society groups on moving the money from the military budgets and military spending (of states and military alliances) towards sustainable, environmental, gender and socio-economic justice.
Goal 3: FEMINIST ALTERNATIVES: "We envision a future where systems of oppression are replaced with feminist alternatives that champion human rights, demilitarisation, accountability, and restitution, and where a just, ecological transition has been achieved, led by economic policies that prioritise the well-being of people and the planet".
Objectives
- Advance a just transition towards ecological sustainability, and a fossil fuel and nuclear free future. - Demilitarise the crisis and security responses, led by properly trained and resourced civilian disaster response efforts. - State and non-state actors uphold human rights norms and legal instruments. - Advance on replacing neoliberal economic policies with investments focused on public resources and basic human needs, and achieving decolonisation through the acknowledgment and transformation of unequal power relations rooted in colonisation and imperialism.
PROGRESS MARKERS 3.1 WILPF IS integrated, intersectional, feminist analysis and actions on militarism, environment and political economy influence policy and decision making at local, regional and global levels. 3.2 WILPF IS has enhanced engagements and collaborations with new actors, spaces and institutions on advocating for feminist solutions to ongoing crises and breakdown of systems. 3.3 WILPF IS's efforts contribute to making the UN institutions and bodies more transparent, inclusive and accountable to people. 3.4 WILPF IS's advocacy and actions contributed to full, equal and meaningful participation of women from all backgrounds at all levels and stages of peace, political and other major (national or multilateral) processes.
Goal 4: POWERFUL MOVEMENT: "Feminist activism underpins the success of each of our first three goals. We envision a powerful, inclusive, and intersectional feminist movement that connects peace activists and other social justice movements on a global scale as we pursue collective action for change".
Objectives:
- Strengthen feminist organising in local, community, and grassroots settings. - Women and feminist activists have effective opportunities to bring the realities of conflict to the attention of decision- makers. - A safe and enabling environment that will ensure activists can continue their advocacy for peace without fear of threats or attacks. - There is wide support and proper resourcing for womens and feminist organisations.
PROGRESS MARKERS 4.1 WILPF has grown and strengthened its network internally and externally on feminist movement building. 4.2 Feminist movement building is advanced due to mutual support and collaborations between IS, Sections, Groups and Partners. 4.3 WILPF IS is able to provide collective care and protection to its Sections, Groups, Partners and activists in times of crises and conflicts. 4.4 WILPF IS creates brave spaces and platforms to foster feminist exchange and learning, and amplify feminist voices and agendas on various thematic positions, contributions and priorities. 4.5 Effective and efficient policies, procedures and operations are in place that strengthen WILPF as an organisation and as well as the global movement, holding itself mutually accountable and living up to its values and vision. 4.6 WILPF IS is able to create a decolonial, anti-racist and safe, secure and inclusive environment for all WILPF members (IS, IB, Sections, Groups and Partners) through the mitigation and addressal of discrimination and structural power within the WILPF movement.

The Women's International League for Peace and Freedom är en global kvinnorättsorganisation som grundades 1915. WILPF arbetar för att uppnå feministisk fred för jämlikhet, rättvisa och en avmilitariserad säkerhet genom en tudelad men sammankopplad ansats: genom att adressera grundorsaker till våld med en feministik ansats och genom att mobilisera för ickevåldsam aktion. WILPF är en medlemsbaserad organisation med aktiva sektioner i ett 50-tal länder världen runt. Sida bidrar med kärnstöd till WILPF:s internationella sekretariat i Geneve baserat på WILPF:s internationella strategi för 2022-2025 samt 2026-2029.

The Women’s International League for Peace and Freedom is a global women's rights organisation, which was founded in 1915. WILPF works to advance feminist peace for equality, justice, and demilitarised security by way of two interlinked paths: by addressing the root causes of violence with a feminist lens and by mobilising for nonviolent action. WILPF is a membership organization with active sections in around 50 countries around the world. Sida provides core support to the WILPF International Secretariat in Geneva based on the WILPF International Strategy 2022-2025 and 2026-2029. Sida’s support is earmarked to ODA-eligible activities and supporting work exclusively in ODA-eligible countries

description.narrative:
Some highlights of results from 2024 in relation to the prioritized countries and sub-tematic focus of Swedish development cooperation under the peace strategy:
- During 2024 WILPF has continued to build on the results they have achieved within area of advocacy efforts linked to arms trade, human rights law, and disarmament. WILPF continues to consistently push for integration of gender, feminist and anti-militarist perspectives into disarmament forums, including in relation to the Arms Trade Treaty (ATT). In collaboration with the ATT Secretariat, in 2022, WILPF contributed to development of a section of the ATT Implementation Guide focused on gender-based violence (GBV). This guide has been shared with ATT States Parties, with particular attention to building expertise in the Global South. Building on these progresses, in February 2024, WILPF delivered a presentation to the ATT Working Group on Transparency and Reporting, offering recommendations on how States Parties can incorporate gender considerations into their reporting practices. In 2024, WILPF also made legal submissions to the UN Human Rights Committee and Arms Trade Treaty forums opposing arms transfers to Isreal. By weaving human rights perspectives into disarmament discussions, WILPF has ensured sustained advocacy at the UN Human Rights Council through statements, reports, and strategic interventions.
- In Ukraine, Sida's core support enabled WILPF to sustain a long-term presence and to support women's organisations and feminist activists to start shaping feminist political economy-informed inputs to reconstruction and recovery discussions, in particular by centering unpaid and underpaid care labour, social reproduction, and gendered survival strategies. Concretely, WILPF brought these feminist- informed priorities into policy spaces within the Ukrainian government in 2024, where women activists and officials engaged in conversations on reconstruction approaches. These dialogues combined policy discussion with empowering and healing practices as women included in the conversations also battled with trauma and insecurities related to their everyday lives. The summary of these conversations has been published, with additional academic papers under review. At the international level, WILPF carried this work into advocacy missions in New York, Washington, D.C., and Brussels, where findings were shared directly with UN Permanent Missions, U.S. policymakers, and EU institutions, embedding feminist reconstruction language into those conversations. At CSW68, where the priority theme was poverty and social protection, WILPF promoted feminist approaches to reconstruction in meetings with ambassadors, side events, and joint advocacy with partners such as ICAN, GPPAC, and NORAD. In addition, WILPF has partnered up with the Graduate Institute, Kharkiv National University, and the Center for Social and Labour Research (CSLR), on a three-year academic collaboration focused on capturing gendered survival practices, circuits of violence, and the political economy of recovery. WILPF leads the component on reconstruction and recovery within the project contributing to development of policy-oriented research that, once finalized, will target both international and Ukrainian policy makers. The project marks a critical step in translating feminist analysis into grounded, policy work strengthening the case for alternative, care-Centered approaches to post-war reconstruction in Ukraine and beyond. Together, these examples show how feminist-informed language and approaches have entered both national dialogues in Ukraine, international bodies (UN, EU, OSCE, CSW), and academia through adopted discourse and policy framing on post-war reconstruction.
- Sida's core grant enabled WILPF to rapidly adapt advocacy and operation responses to dynamic crises (e.g. in Gaza, Lebanon, Afghanistan, Ukraine, among others), and to develop cross-thematic analysis to influence policy discussions and advocacy efforts. This level of adaptability allowed WILPF to operate strategically across interconnected domains of peace, rights, and justice. It also helped avoid fragmented, short-term programming and enabled long-term movement-building that centre local ownership and feminist transformation. In Lebanon for example, WILPF's support allowed partners like the "The Knowledge Workshop" to repurpose their office into a a relief coordination hub, reallocate funds to support grassroots organizers, and retain key staff during peak instability. Similarly in Palestine, partners were able to continue their feminist political work under siege conditions by reallocating resources, adjusting timelines, and maintaining community presence despite dire circumstances. Rather than defaulting to fragmented emergency responses, WILPF's holistic resourcing model allowed partners to remain rooted, politically relevant, and structurally resilient. These adaptations illustrate a broader feminist sustainability approach, where funding is not only flexible, but enables care- based infrastructure, institutional continutity, and the capacity for long-term transformation, even under ongoing violence.
